question: Can the exact charge-prefix affinity contract throughout the square bulk, before any charge adjacent to the logical cut is revealed?
scope: Canonical square graph with independent ternary edge currents, physical signed charges, rough boundary vertices unmeasured, and right-boundary cut parity H. Fixed 0<p<1 and any finite link field or edge-wise orientation bias preserving edge independence. This is an all-size structural statement, not a thermodynamic phase classification.

competing_outcomes.bulk_independent: Bulk charge depends on edge currents disjoint from the logical cut, so its entire joint record is independent of H and prefix affinity is unchanged.
competing_outcomes.bulk_informative: An incidence or measurement convention couples bulk charge to cut currents, invalidating the disjoint-edge argument.

method: Prove independence from disjoint edge sigma-algebras; verify canonical geometry at the already-used L=3,5,7,11 sizes and compare the exact L=3 initial affinity against the retained H12 result. No current enumeration or stochastic sampling.
observables: number of measured bulk and cut-adjacent charge vertices
intersection of bulk incidence edges and logical cut edges
initial sector affinity discrepancy against retained L=3 exact data
acceptance: Every checked geometry has zero bulk-cut incidence overlap; all cut edges touch exactly one measured strip vertex and one unmeasured rough vertex; retained L=3 F_0 matches sqrt(pi_0 pi_1) to 1e-12. Then record the all-size proof, Bayes-risk consequence, and limitation that cut-adjacent strip charges remain unresolved.
stop_rule: Stop and fail closed on any geometry or retained-evidence mismatch. Do not infer a p=.30 phase or extrapolate the strip contraction.
literature_basis: The product-current and physical signed-charge observation are the already registered Lab 006/007 model; this transition derives a model-specific conditional-independence corollary, not a borrowed threshold theorem.
